profile.name: Javed Qadir Bakhsh
profile.headline: A Life of Public Service, Christian Leadership and Preservation of History
profile.guidingPrinciple: Preserve history for the coming generations.

blocks.p: Javed Qadir Bakhsh is a Pakistani public servant, Christian leader, Formanite, and historian whose life has been shaped by three enduring commitments: service to the nation, service to the Church, and preservation of history for future generations.

His journey encompasses Christian student leadership, a distinguished career in the Government of Pakistan, international professional training, and decades of active participation in the life and administration of the Church of Pakistan.

In 1962, following his father’s transfer from Christ Church, Drigh Road, Karachi, to the Central Cathedral of Praying Hands, Lahore, a new chapter began in his life. He moved to Lahore with his family and was admitted to Cathedral School, Hall Road. It was here that his formative years of education and character development took shape. He completed his Matriculation in 1969, laying the foundation for the remarkable journey of faith, service and leadership that would follow.

sections.title: Forman Christian College — The Beginning of Leadership

blocks.p: Javed Qadir Bakhsh is a proud Formanite, having graduated from Forman Christian College, Lahore, in 1974, and completed his postgraduate studies in 1976.
During his student years, he was actively involved in the Student Christian Movement (SCM) and served as:

list: Student Secretary, National Student Christian Movement

blocks.p: His student leadership provided an important foundation for his later service to the Church and to the wider community.
After completing his education, Javed Qadir Bakhsh entered the Government of Pakistan and pursued a career devoted to public service.
He ultimately served as Joint Census Commissioner, Government of Pakistan, contributing to the country's national census and demographic administration.
His professional responsibilities required a high degree of accuracy, organisation and understanding of population data—information essential for national planning and development.

A particularly significant milestone in his public-service career came in 1989, when Javed Qadir Bakhsh earned and qualified for a scholarship offered by the Government of Pakistan under the Bush Scholarship programme.
Under this scholarship, he travelled to the United States of America for professional exposure and training at the U.S. Census Bureau in Washington, D.C.

His association with the U.S. Census Bureau provided him with an opportunity to observe and learn from one of the world's leading institutions in population census administration, demographic statistics and census methodology.
The experience broadened his professional knowledge and brought an important international dimension to his work with the Government of Pakistan.
His selection for the scholarship was also a recognition of his professional capabilities and contribution to Pakistan's census administration.
He was in charge of the Population Census Organization, Punjab province. It is the biggest province of Pakistan.
Besides this, he headed the Coordination Department in Islamabad.
He has vast experience of field operations of the biggest data collection and analysing agency in Pakistan.

sections.title: Service to the Church of Pakistan

blocks.p: Alongside his government career, Javed Qadir Bakhsh remained deeply involved in the life and administration of the Church of Pakistan.
His Church service has included responsibilities at parish, diocesan and national levels.

list: Executive Committee (Church of Pakistan) — Served as a member of the Executive Committee of the Church of Pakistan, participating in matters relating to the wider administration and affairs of the united Church.
Parish Committee — Served as a member of the Parish Committee, contributing to parish administration and community life.
Clergy Ordination Committee (Diocese of Raiwind) — Served on the Diocesan Clergy Ordination Committee, contributing to matters concerning candidates for ordained ministry.
Education Board — Served on the Education Board, reflecting his continuing interest in Christian education and institutional development.

blocks.p: These responsibilities demonstrate a sustained commitment to the governance, education, clergy development and institutional life of the Church.
One of the defining features of Javed Qadir Bakhsh's continuing work has been his passion for preserving the history of the Church of Pakistan and the Christian community in Pakistan.
He has devoted considerable attention to documenting the formation and development of the Church, its dioceses, bishops, clergy, lay leaders and institutions.
He believes that history is not merely a record of dates and events. It is the collective memory of a community.
His particular concern is that the contributions of clergy, lay people, students and Christian institutions should be properly recorded so that they are not lost with the passing of generations.

blocks.subheading: Preserving the Role of the Laity

blocks.p: Javed Qadir Bakhsh has also shown a strong interest in documenting and strengthening the role of the laity in the Church.

His own experience of Christian student leadership and later participation in Church committees has given him an appreciation of the importance of meaningful cooperation between clergy and lay members.
He believes that responsible participation by lay people strengthens the Church and contributes to transparent, effective and representative Church administration.

blocks.subheading: Preserving the Legacy of Bishop Johnston Safdar Qadir Bakhsh

blocks.p: Another important part of his historical work is the preservation of the life and legacy of his father, Bishop Johnston Safdar Qadir Bakhsh, a pioneering leader of the Church of Pakistan.
Through biographical research, historical documentation and the collection of memories and records, Javed seeks to preserve his father's contribution for future generations.
This work is both a family tribute and part of a wider effort to preserve the history of the early Church of Pakistan and the generation of leaders who helped shape it.
Javed Qadir Bakhsh's life represents a bridge between generations.

From his student leadership at Forman Christian College, through his professional career in the Government of Pakistan and his international experience at the U.S. Census Bureau, to his continuing service in the Church of Pakistan, his journey has remained rooted in leadership, service and responsibility.
He believes that younger generations should have access to the stories, documents, photographs and experiences of those who came before them.
His guiding principle is:

blocks.quote: Preserve history for the coming generations.

blocks.p: Four major themes characterise his journey:

list: Education — Forman Christian College and postgraduate studies.
Student Leadership — General Secretary of the Student Christian Movement and Student Secretary of the National SCM.

Public Service — A distinguished career in the Government of Pakistan culminating in service as Joint Census Commissioner, including international professional exposure at the U.S. Census Bureau through the Bush Scholarship in 1989.

Christian and Historical Service — Continuing involvement in the Church of Pakistan through the Executive Committee, Parish Committee, Clergy Ordination Committee and Education Board, together with his work to preserve Christian history.

blocks.p: Javed Qadir Bakhsh's continuing mission is to ensure that the history of Christian institutions and communities in Pakistan is recorded, preserved and made available to future generations.

blocks.emphasis: His work seeks to bring together:
People • Places • Institutions • Documents • Photographs • Memories • Church Records • Personal Testimonies

blocks.p: so that an important part of Pakistan's Christian heritage is not forgotten.

Javed Qadir Bakhsh has created a Facebook page, “History: Church of Pakistan,” through which he shares photographs and memories of clergy, lay leaders, and other people who have served the Church of Pakistan. His aim is to preserve the contributions of church leaders and keep the history of the Church alive for present and future generations.

He also shares facts, figures, and historical information from the official minutes and records of the Church, making this valuable material accessible to a wider audience and helping people understand and remember the Church’s journey.
In addition, he has initiated two programmes on Facebook:

list: Rab Ki Khidmat (Service of the Spirit) — focusing on faith, Christian service, and spiritual encouragement.
Motivational Programmes for Youngsters — designed to encourage and inspire young people in their personal, professional, and spiritual journeys.

blocks.p: As part of the motivational programme, he would like to interview young professionals and successful young Pakistanis, giving them an opportunity to share their experiences, challenges, achievements, and lessons learned. The purpose is to inspire and motivate the younger generation and show them positive examples of young people making a meaningful contribution to society.
His vision is to preserve the past, celebrate those who served, and inspire the younger generation to build a better future.

The life of Javed Qadir Bakhsh is a story of continuing service—from student Christian leadership to national public service, from international professional experience to Church administration, and from personal family history to the preservation of a wider Christian heritage.
His journey reflects a simple conviction:

blocks.quote: Service is a responsibility, and history is a legacy.

blocks.p: He believes that we preserve history not simply to remember the past, but to give future generations the knowledge and wisdom they need to understand their heritage and build upon it.
